exposure: Inflammatory bowel disease activity during pregnancy
cohort: The study included 100 consecutive patients with Inflammatory Bowel Disease (81 with Crohn's Disease, 19 with Ulcerative Colitis) and their 235 pregnancies followed up at Amiens University Hospital between 2007 and 2021.
finding: Women with active Inflammatory Bowel Disease during pregnancy were more likely to experience hospital admission, premature delivery, very premature delivery, shorter term at birth, lower birth weight, and a higher caesarean section rate compared to those with inactive disease.
mod_finding: Patients with active disease had a higher caesarean section rate (54.2% vs. 16.9%) compared to those with inactive disease.
birth_weight: Active IBD group: 2707 g; Inactive IBD group: 3129 g
gest_age: Active IBD group: 36.77 WA (premature delivery) and 38.4 WA (term at birth); Inactive IBD group: 38.7 WA (premature delivery) and 39.8 WA (term at birth)
